stories.headline: Brent edges up to [$92.6] on Riyadh attacks
stories.summary: Brent crude rose 59 cents, or 0.6%, to $92.57 a barrel on Friday morning, 20 Nov, and December WTI gained 0.5% to $83.63. Houthi missile attacks on Riyadh revived Middle East supply worries. Still, Brent is set for a 3.5% weekly fall as Hormuz crude shipments return to near pre-war levels.

stories.headline: Hormuz attacks [one a day] - 2 seafarers missing
stories.summary: Attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz are running at roughly one a day, with about 14 incidents so far in November, UKMTO says. At least two seafarers are missing after attacks this week. ADNOC says one crew member is still unaccounted for and 11 were injured on its tanker. Kuwait has told the IMO eight of its tankers were attacked.

stories.headline: Bayesian report: crew [never knew wind risk]
stories.summary: Britain's MAIB says the 56-metre superyacht Bayesian's vulnerability to wind had never been assessed, so its crew were unaware of the risk. The yacht capsized and sank in about 18 minutes after a violent downburst off Porticello, Sicily, in August 2024. Seven people died, including tech tycoon Mike Lynch and his daughter Hannah.

stories.headline: Houston pilot faces [manslaughter charge] over collision
stories.summary: Ship pilot Darris Jefferson, 39, has been indicted on a federal seaman's manslaughter charge, the first case of its kind against a pilot. He was conning bulk carrier Yangze 7 when it hit towboat Miss Peggy in the Houston Ship Channel in July 2024. Deckhand Aquarius Lowman, 25, died. NTSB found a 39-minute phone call distracted him.

stories.headline: LA-Long Beach port strike [could start Saturday]
stories.summary: About 250 port security workers of ILWU Local 26 could walk off the job from 12:01 a.m. Saturday, 21 Nov, when their contract extension ends. Their six terminals handle about 85% of Long Beach cargo and 33% of Los Angeles cargo. Other dockworkers are expected to honour picket lines. Talks resume on Friday.

stories.headline: Samsung to build [nuclear-powered LNG carrier]
stories.summary: Samsung Heavy Industries and Norway's Tesser Atomics signed an exclusive deal on 19 Nov to develop the first nuclear-powered LNG carrier. It would use Tesser's Triton salt-cooled reactor with TRISO fuel. The demonstration ship is expected to trade commercially between the United States and Europe. No size, price or delivery date was given.

stories.headline: US LNG ships [U-turn to Europe] as prices rise
stories.summary: More US LNG cargoes are diverting to Europe as the market there tightens, ship-tracking by Kpler shows. Al Qassar turned west from Egypt's Port Said and Amaryllis Knutsen made a U-turn near Egypt. Two other US-loaded ships turned north from Asia. Asian LNG now trades at a discount to European prices.

stories.headline: TEN posts [record $403m] profit, doubles dividend
stories.summary: Greek tanker owner TEN Ltd reported record nine-month net income of $403 million, up 355%, on revenues of $851 million. Third-quarter profit was $174.5 million. It doubled its next semi-annual dividend to $1.00 a share. TEN booked $94 million gains from selling four ships and has a 20-vessel newbuilding programme.

stories.headline: Samsung Heavy wins [$245m] LNG carrier order
stories.summary: Samsung Heavy Industries won an order for one LNG carrier worth 342.4 billion won, about $245 million, from a shipowner in Oceania, for delivery by July 2029. The yard has now taken 49 ships worth $12.7 billion this year, 91% of its annual target, including 21 LNG carriers.
